newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Carlson to expand UK travel agencies.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Carlson to expand UK travel agencies.

text.p: Carlson Leisure Group (UK) plans to expand its UK travel agency chain after its agreed bid for package holiday firm Inspirations Plc, chairman Michael Batt said on Thursday.
"We intend to grow our retail presence and we will re-brand the stores next year," Batt said in a telephone interview.
CLG (UK), part of Carlson Companies Inc of Minneapolis, operates 409 travel agency shops under the AT Mays brand, 97 of which are owned by Inspirations.
Britain's Office of Fair Trading last year launched an inquiry into vertical integration in the industry, the results of which have yet to be disclosed.
Leading tour operators Thomson and Airtours have their own travel agency chains, Thomson owning the Lunn Poly chain and Airtours operating the Going Places stores.
Batt would not comment on the inquiry but said that Carlson's plans should boost competition in the high street and the enlarged company would offer better value to customers.
Carlson said its long-term intention was to seek a European partner to take a controlling stake in Inspirations' charter airline Caledonian and a significant interest in CLG (UK).
Such a move would satisfy EU rules on the licensing of air carriers and also provide a financial partner to participate in the development of CLG (UK).
The bid from CLG (UK) values Inspirations at around 42 million stg. The Carlson group of companies includes the Radisson hotel chain and a franchising network of T.G.I. Friday's restaurants.
